name: attention-catchup-latency
definition: For each nightly reaction run, the gap in days between the run's own date and `attention_day` (the newest committed day in foreknown/reaction/attention/), and whether the immediately-preceding day was retried and still failed with 'not published yet'. practice/src/practice/foreknown/reaction.py (run_reaction, lines 292-320) retries every missing day between the backfill horizon and yesterday on every run, not only the newest one, so a failed day is not lost — but if the notary consistently runs before GDELT's daily file for the prior day is published, the gap could sit at 2 days indefinitely rather than the 1-day lag the code's own comment expects ('GDELT publishes a day's file the following morning'). Across the two nights so far: 2026-08-08's reading shows attention_day=2026-08-07 with zero failures (that run never attempted 2026-08-08, since days_before() only generates days strictly before the run's own date); 2026-08-09's reading also shows attention_day=2026-08-07, this time after one attempt at 2026-08-08 that failed 'not published yet' (foreknown/reaction/readings/2026-08-09.json, failures). attention_days_committed has not grown past 60 in either recorded night.
test_rule: On each nightly reaction run, compute gap_days = (run date - attention_day). Record, per run, whether the immediately-preceding day (run date minus 1) is present in attention_days_committed, absent-and-untried, or absent-with-a-'not published yet'-failure this run. The sensor fires once N=5 consecutive nights show the same day-of-run gap_days value with a 'not published yet' failure recorded each time for the newest missing day — evidence that the notary's fixed run time structurally precedes GDELT's publication time for that day, rather than an occasional miss. N=5 chosen to match roughly one working week, long enough to rule out a one-off GDELT outage (the reaction reading's own failures list already distinguishes 'not published yet' from other HTTP errors, so this sensor only needs to count that one failure string, not diagnose new failure modes).
falsification: Falsified if, once more nights exist, the gap closes on its own within a night or two after appearing (i.e. a day fetched successfully on the run right after its first 'not published yet') rather than recurring every night at the same offset — that would mean the two-night pattern seen so far is normal catch-up latency, not a structural mismatch between the notary's run time and GDELT's publish time, and this sensor should not fire. Also falsified, independent of the pattern, if the notary's run time itself is not fixed (e.g. it moves with GitHub Actions/cloud-routine scheduling jitter) — the test_rule assumes a roughly constant run time, which autonomy/log.jsonl's own foreknown-notary-run timestamps (2026-08-08T17:40:13+00:00, 2026-08-09T06:27:05+00:00, a roughly 11-hour shift already between the only two nights recorded) do not yet confirm as stable.
